full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is starting to come into view, which means more NFL futures are being released with each passing week. I broke down the [2026 NFL MVP Odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-mvp-odds#/) earlier this offseason, and it’s time to dive into the 2026 Offensive Player of the Year odds.

__Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ didn’t even start the season on BetMGM’s betting board for the Offensive Player of the Year before eventually capturing the honor. He finished with 119/1793/10 receiving for the NFC’s top-seeded Seahawks. He narrowly beat out __Christian McCaffrey__, who totaled 2126/17 scrimmage, and __Puka Nacua__, who posted 129/1715/10 receiving, for the honor. __Bijan Robinson__ (+900 odds) is the favorite to win this year’s award after finishing fourth in voting last season. He’s followed closely by contenders like __Jahmyr Gibbs__ (+1000), __Ja’Marr Chase__ (+1200), Nacua (+1200), and JSN (+1500) at 15/1 odds or shorter.

\>Be sure to check out [Brolley’s Best Bets: 2026 NFL Futures](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/series/2025/best-bets) for my favorite futures bets all offseason…Subscribe to the Best Bets Podcast on your [favorite platform](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/podcasts/show/nfl-best-bets) and on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@FantasyPointsBetting) for year-round NFL betting talk…Join our “#official-bets” [Fantasy Points Discord](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/discord) to see our staff's wagers as soon as we make them!

Recent History Tells Us…
------------------------

The voters have decided to award the OPOY to the best non-quarterback skill player based on recent seasons, which coincides with the MVP becoming an exclusive award for quarterbacks — QBs have won the MVP in 13 consecutive seasons. Quarterbacks have won 20 times since the award’s inception in 1972, but __Patrick Mahomes__ was the last QB to claim the honor seven seasons ago when he threw for 50 TDs in his first season as a starter. Wide receivers and running backs have each won the award four times over the last decade, with WRs holding a 4-3 edge over RBs since the last QB victory in 2018.

We have historical odds for this award for the last five years, and a mixture of longshots and favorites have claimed the honor. __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ didn’t even have preseason odds at BetMGM before exploding for 1793 yards last season, and __Cooper Kupp__ came from way off the pack at +8000 odds in 2021. __Justin Jefferson__ (+1200), __Christian McCaffrey__ (+1500), and __Saquon Barkley__ (+2200) each ranked in the top 10 in odds when they won the award in 2022-24.

The Offensive Player of the Year also must be a major contributor to his team winning 11 or more games. __Adrian Peterson__ was the last winner to fail to reach 11+ victories in 2012, when the Vikings won 10 games.

Bets I Considered
-----------------

### __{{Jahmyr Gibbs|RB|DET|23200}}__ (+1000, FanDuel)

+ __Why I like Gibbs__: Detroit traded David Montgomery to the Texans, and the Lions will turn to Isiah Pacheco as the #2 option, who’s a clear downgrade from Montgomery. Pacheco struggled to keep Kareem Hunt off the field, especially in goal-line situations, which bodes well for Gibbs receiving a massive workload in his first season without Monty in the backfield. Pacheco settled for a one-year deal worth just $1.8 million because of his declining play and his lack of pedigree, and he’ll have to earn his roster spot in training camp. Gibbs averaged 32.6 FPG and 162.4 scrimmage YPG in three games missed by Monty in 2024. He also led the NFL with 24.7 FPG and averaged 121.3 scrimmage YPG from Week 10 on last season, which coincided with Dan Campbell taking over playcalling and leaning more heavily on Gibbs. Detroit’s offense has ranked in the top five in PPG and YPG for four straight seasons, and Gibbs will be a big reason if they remain one of the NFL’s best offenses once again.

+ __Why I ultimately passed__: Gibbs’ odds are a little too short at +1000 odds for me to make this wager, especially for an award that tends to be a little more wide open than the MVP race. He has stiff competition for the honor from his own teammate, Amon-Ra St. Brown, who has the 13th-best odds to win the OPOY. Gibbs and ARSB have the shortest odds of any teammates, and I’d be slightly concerned about splitting votes and credit for Detroit’s offensive success this season. The Lions were also concerned enough about their offensive line’s decline in recent seasons to slightly reach for offensive tackle Blake Miller at 17th overall.

### __{{Jaxon Smith-Njigba|WR|SEA|23157}}__ (+1500, BetMGM)

+ __Why I like JSN__: He’s the defending Offensive Player of the Year, yet he finds himself down the board a bit as the fifth favorite for the award. JSN blew away all other receivers in receiving yards (1793), target share (36.1%), and air yards share (49.1%) during his third-year breakout campaign. The offense could revolve around him even more this season after Kenneth Walker left for Kansas City in free agency. He turned just 24 years old less than a week after winning the Super Bowl, so there’s a chance we haven’t even seen JSN’s best football just yet.
+ __Why I ultimately passed__: JSN will likely have to blow away the field to win the OPOY for the second straight season because he could face some voter fatigue after winning a tight race last year. Marshall Faulk was the last player to win in consecutive seasons when he won three straight times in 1999-2001, and Earl Campbell in 1978-80 was the only other player to win in consecutive seasons. I also worry about Seattle’s offense taking a step back with Klint Kubiak leaving for Las Vegas and Brian Fleury taking over playcalling.

### __{{Ladd McConkey|WR|LAC|25097}}__ (+15000, DraftKings)

+ __Why I like McConkey__: Ryan Heath [laid out the case](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/finding-the-next-jaxon-smith-njigba-playcaller-tendencies#/) for several WRs to be the next Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and McConkey had one of the best cases as Mike McDaniel takes over the playcalling. Collins wasn’t left off the betting board like __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ was last preseason at BetMGM. Still, he’s an overlooked third-round fantasy selection on a team that could win a lot of games with an alpha receiver leading the offense and one of the NFL’s best defenses. Collins will get most of the credit if he has a monster season after __C.J. Stroud__’s shaky postseason performances significantly lowered his national approval rating at the position, a lot like what __Sam Darnold__ did in his final two games of the 2024 season in Minnesota.

Collins’ biggest issue has been staying healthy for an entire season, which he’s yet to do in his first five years. He’s missed nine games since breaking out in 2023, and he’s failed to reach half the snaps in another four games over that span. Collins has been one of the NFL’s best receivers when he’s healthy over the last three seasons, averaging 5.4 receptions and 86.1 receiving YPG in the 38 games he’s played more than half of the snaps. Collins has been knocking on the door to finish among the receiving league leaders, and, with a little better injury luck, he could do it as he enters just his age-27 season.

The Texans are another team that could move toward more two-WR personnel, which would give Collins weaker competition for targets with fewer WRs on the field. The Texans deployed 11 personnel at the highest rate (69.8%), but they drafted __Marlin Klein__ in the second round and handed __Foster Moreau__ $6.3 million guaranteed in free agency. Collins certainly needs Stroud to play better than he has the last two years. He’s capable of it, having played at an elite level during his rookie season, and the Texans did their best to get him moving in the right direction by upgrading his offensive line. Collins could be the top offensive weapon on one of the NFL’s best teams. The Texans are the favorites to win the AFC South at +115 odds (46.5% implied odds), and Houston sits at +145 odds (40.8%) to win 11 or more games at DraftKings Sportsbook.

full_text:
The NFL is into “Phase Three” of the offseason, the final stage before contact practices begin with training camp in late July. We’ve seen a steady stream of news since OTAs (organized team activities) started in mid-May, and it always gets a little more interesting in June when veteran players are required to report for one mandatory minicamp unless they have an excused absence.

I went team by team to round up the most important fantasy headlines coming out of all 32 workouts. I’ll update this article through June 18, the final day of team activities in Phase Three. Check back often for regular updates!

\>Each news item will have a date at the end of it for when it was updated or added to the article…ADP data used in this article is based on the last month of drafts with our partners over at [Underdog Fantasy](https://www.fantasypoints.com/underdog#/)…Subscribe to our [Fantasy Bundle Package](https://www.fantasypoints.com/plans#/) to take your NFL research to the next level!

{{CTA|Underdog|omit=\[none\]}}

__AFC East__
------------

#### Buffalo Bills

+   __Dalton Kincaid__ has flashed massive fantasy potential early in his career, but he’s been a part-time player in Buffalo’s offense and has been unable to stay healthy. A healthy Kincaid could go a long way to getting him on the field more in 2026. He owns just a 57% route share in 42 of a possible 51 career games since the Bills selected him in the first round in 2023. Kincaid opted against surgery to fix his PCL injury from last season, electing to rehab the injury based on the recommendations of the doctors he talked to about his condition. He [said his knee feels better](https://x.com/NickSabatoGNN/status/2056839766138569038?s=20), which was helped by adding 10-to-12 pounds of muscle this offseason. Kincaid led the league in TPRR (.27) and YPRR (3.19) among 53 TEs who ran 150+ routes, but he ranked seventh in route share (44.2%) among Bills receivers — he even ranked behind __Dawson Knox__ at 48.2%. I’ve been hoping that Kincaid could stay healthy and run more routes since he broke into the league, but it hasn’t happened yet heading into his fourth season. It seems unlikely that __Joe Brady__ changes his approach at TE as he moves from offensive coordinator to head coach. It’s still worth taking a shot on Kincaid at his depressed ADP (131, TE13) because he has top-five potential at the position if he could ever get close to a 70% route share. *(Added May 20)*

+   __Josh Allen__ is participating in Buffalo’s offseason program as he promised after undergoing surgery in late January to remove a bone chip from his right foot. A healthy Allen is getting some initial work in with his new receiver, __DJ Moore__, who is coming off the worst season of his career before getting traded to the Bills. Allen is the clear QB1 this draft season with an ADP of 30, and he’s going a full two rounds earlier than the QB2, __Lamar Jackson__. *(Added May 20)*

#### New England Patriots

+   __Kayshon Boutte__ has been working out [away from the team](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48780703/new-england-patriots-notebook-longest-tenured-employee-nancy-meier-retire) facility during New England’s voluntary offseason program, which is a sign he could still be on the trade block after the Patriots were reportedly shopping him before and during the draft. It’s worth selecting Boutte in the final rounds of your best ball drafts if you picked __Jalen Hurts__ in the sixth or seventh round, since there’s a good chance Boutte and a future first-round pick could be coming to Philadelphia in exchange for Brown. *(Added May 20)*

#### Cleveland Browns

+   __Quinshon Judkins__ participated in voluntary minicamp in late April and in voluntary OTA workouts on May 20, which is five months after he suffered a dislocated ankle and a fractured fibula, which required surgery on Dec. 23. His initial recovery timeline called for 4-6 months off before returning to football activity, so it appears he’s on track to be ready for training camp. Judkins and __Cam Skattebo__ are both returning from fractured fibulas. Ryan Heath [laid out](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2056752913913991666) how players returning from similar injuries have been fantasy potholes in the recent past. Judkins is looking to break that trend behind a revamped offensive line in __Todd Monken__’s new offense. He should rack up plenty of carries to justify selecting him as an RB2 at his fifth-round ADP (55, RB23), but it’s tough to build a massive upside case since he could lose passing-game snaps to __Dylan Sampson__ in what is shaping up to be a spread offense. *(Added May 20)*

+   The Browns are laying the early groundwork to name __Deshaun Watson__ as the Week 1 starter over __Shedeur Sanders__ once training camp rolls around. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler [heard](https://x.com/ESPNCleveland/status/2056121255984566332?s=20) Watson has “hit it off with __Todd Monken__”, and Mary Kay Cabot [reported](https://x.com/MaryKayCabot/status/2049523640450871504?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet) in late April that Watson took the lead over Sanders. The decision to go with Watson is also another indication that Monken’s offense could be more of a spread attack than his TE-heavy attack in Baltimore. The Browns already selected __KC Concepcion__ and __Denzel Boston__ inside the top 39 picks to bolster their WR depth, and Watson previously struggled in __Kevin Stefanski__’s under-center offense. Watson is entering the final year of his disastrous five-year, $230 million contract he signed in 2022, and the Browns clearly want to take one final look at Watson since they’re paying him so much money. The Browns can also ice the Shedeur hype early in the season, but he’ll eventually get opportunities to play later in the season once Watson flames out. *(Added May 19)*

#### Pittsburgh Steelers

+   The Steelers and __Aaron Rodgers__ finally came to terms on a one-year, $22 million guaranteed deal that is worth up to $25 million. He said on May 20 that this upcoming season would be his last, but he admitted he thought 2025 would be his final season after __Mike Tomlin__ stepped away before being drawn back in by the Steelers hiring __Mike McCarthy__. Rodgers wanted the ball out of his hands last season, finishing with the fastest average time to throw (2.38 seconds) and the fourth-lowest aDOT (6.3 yards) among 45 QBs who attempted 100+ passes. The style of play led him to rank 10th in catchable throw rate (76.9%) and fourth in turnover-worthy throw rate (1.6%), but 31st in hero throw rate (3.8%). He’s posted a solid 4.8% TD rate in each of his last three healthy campaigns, but he’s unlikely to do much better at 42 years old. The Steelers at least added __Michael Pittman__ and __Germie Bernard__ to a receiving corps that ranked 31st in 11 personnel (38.9%) under playcaller __Arthur Smith__. Rodgers will step into a familiar offense under his longtime Packers HC, whose offense ranked ninth in 11 personnel (70.8%) in his final season with the Cowboys. Rodgers won two of his four MVPs under McCarthy, but those days are long gone. He should at least have a little more upside than his QB27 (14.7) from last season, with a better receiving corps around him. *(Updated May 20)*

#### Kansas City Chiefs

+   __Rashee Rice__ is once again in trouble with the law. He triggered a 30-day jail sentence by testing positive for THC, which violated his five-year deferred probation for a third-degree felony charge last summer. He’ll miss Chiefs OTAs and mandatory minicamp while he serves jail time until June 16. He faced a six-game suspension to start last season for driving nearly 120 mph and causing a multi-car crash on a Dallas highway in March 2024. The NFL announced in early April that it closed its investigation into abuse allegations and that he wouldn’t face any additional discipline from the league. Rice’s career is on thin ice after his latest misstep, even if he doesn’t face an additional suspension for his latest legal issue. He could face a much longer jail sentence or have his probation revoked completely if he can’t stay out of his own way for the 4+ years remaining on his probation. It also came out that Rice needed to have a clean-up procedure on his right knee a week before he was ordered to serve jail time. Rice’s dynasty value takes another significant hit with the latest news, and he’s a riskier pick for the upcoming season, especially if the Chiefs decide to protect themselves by signing a player like __Stefon Diggs__ in the coming weeks. *(Updated May 20)*

+   GM __Jason Licht__ [said](https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bucs/2026/05/16/bucky-irving-kenneth-gainwell-sean-tucker-rachaad-white-zac-robinson/) __Bucky Irving__ would be limited during OTAs but should be ready for training camp. He suffered a left shoulder injury in Week 4 last season and missed seven straight games due to the issue and an ankle injury. He never regained his form even when he returned to the lineup, and he needed [offseason surgery](https://www.joebucsfan.com/2026/02/bucky-irving-had-offseason-shoulder-surgery/) to repair the lingering shoulder issue. Irving mentally struggled to get over his first major injury, so it shouldn’t be a huge surprise that the Buccaneers are taking it slow with Irving at this time of year. The Buccaneers paid __Kenneth Gainwell__ $9.83 million guaranteed to be a high-end #2 option behind Tampa Bay’s 2024 fourth-round pick. Gainwell has a history of earning a bigger role than expected, and this backfield is setting up to be a potential three-man committee. Bucky is a tough click for me at his current ADP (45, RB18) since he could be a between-the-20s player, with Gainwell stealing passing-game snaps and __Sean Tucker__ vulturing goal-line opportunities. *(Added May 19)*

__NFC West__
------------

#### Arizona Cardinals

+   __Jacoby Brissett__ wasn’t present for the start of Arizona’s voluntary OTAs as he seeks a pay raise on his $4.88 million contract, with just $1.5 million guaranteed for the 2026 season. He’s still being paid like a backup despite the organization [informing him](https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/48810874/without-jacoby-brissett-mike-lafleur-cardinals-open-otas) that he would open the season as the starter. Arizona handed __Gardner Minshew__ $5.14 million in guaranteed money in free agency before selecting __Carson Beck__ at No. 65, so Brissett is unlikely to get a hefty raise before the season. He ranked as the QB7 (19.9 FPG) from Week 6 through the end of the season, but he won’t drop back 45.8 times per game as he did last season. Brissett isn’t the easiest click in best ball drafts, even at this suppressed ADP (178, QB28). The Cards are likely to be out of postseason contention, and they’ll want to take a look at Beck during the best ball money-making weeks. Brissett is much more intriguing in 2-QB/Superflex redraft leagues if you want to punt your second-QB spot until the middle rounds of the draft and use Brissett until he eventually is benched later in the season. *(May 19)*

#### San Francisco 49ers

+   *The Athletic*’s Matt Barrows broke down San Francisco’s receiving corps in a [recent mailbag](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7289584/2026/05/19/49ers-schedule-wide-receivers/). He believes __Mike Evans__ will play the X, __Ricky Pearsall__ will line up at Z, and __Christian Kirk__ and second-round pick __De’Zhaun Stribling__ will compete to be the slot receiver. He also thinks Stribling will train to be the backup X receiver behind Evans, and Kirk will be the backup Z receiver behind Pearsall. Those backup distinctions could be important when we’re working the waiver wire later this year because of Evans’ and Pearsall’s durability issues. Evans missed 10 games the last two seasons, and Pearsall sat out 14 contests in his first two seasons. *(Added May 20)*
